summary:
We have developed ExoVitals, an autonomous Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) and medical HUD designed for deep space exploration missions (Moon Artemis and Mars). Beyond Low Earth Orbit, communication delays of up to 22 minutes and solar conjunction blackouts make real-time telemedicine from Earth impossible.

To address this critical challenge, ExoVitals runs fully offline on an Edge-First architecture (< 1 ms latency), enabling astronauts to monitor vital signs, assess environmental hazards, and detect hidden clinical risks before irreversible damage occurs. Our system evaluates real-time telemetry against NASA’s RIDGE matrix (Radiation, Isolation, Distance, Gravity, and Hostile Environments) and NASA-STD-3001 standards.

The web interface was developed in TypeScript using React and Next.js, featuring an interactive 3D holographic anatomical explorer powered by Three.js and real-time biometric evolution charts. An onboard AI copilot powered by Google Gemini provides deterministic offline-safe emergency triage and generates standardized SBAR medical reports for asynchronous transmission to Mission Control. ExoVitals empowers autonomous astronaut health and ensures crew survivability when Earth is too far to help.
details:
Our project is an autonomous clinical decision support system and real-time medical monitoring HUD that safeguards astronaut health during deep space exploration missions where Earth communication latency prevents traditional telemedicine.

The project's main benefit is providing deep space crews with self-reliant, real-time medical autonomy. By actively tracking physiological shifts and habitat telemetry, the system flags subclinical degradation early—such as bone demineralization and hidden renal stone formation from microgravity, immunosuppression from cosmic radiation, and cognitive impairment from CO2 pockets and sleep fragmentation. It carries a profound human survival and exploration impact, transforming raw biometric sensors into actionable countermeasure prescriptions (resistive exercise, specialized nutrition, and shielding protocols).

To develop the project, we used:

• Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3

• Frameworks & Libraries: Next.js (App Router), React 19, Tailwind CSS, Zustand (high-performance 1Hz atomic state management)

• 3D Graphics & Data Visualization: Three.js, React Three Fiber (@react-three/fiber), React Three Drei (@react-three/drei), Recharts (mission trend analysis), Custom lightweight SVG real-time charts (MiniChart)

• APIs & Storage: Google Gemini API (@google/generative-ai), IndexedDB (idb-keyval for offline persistence), Progressive Web App (Service Worker offline caching)

• Testing & Verification: Vitest, Contract validation scripts (check-contracts.mjs, check-i18n.mjs)

Our approach is creative because it bridges complex aerospace medicine with an intuitive, tactical medical HUD. It combines a 3D holographic body explorer that visually highlights organ stress with a deterministic clinical engine that operates without needing an internet connection. We focused on accessibility, offline reliability, sub-millisecond execution, and dual-language inclusivity (English/Spanish) as core design factors.
